description: Evaluation set for the Summit Roofing inbox agent.

urgency_rubric.high: Active water ingress, storm damage, exposed structure, or a safety risk.
urgency_rubric.medium: A concrete action is waiting on us and carries a time element: scheduling, an external deadline, or a complaint without active damage.
urgency_rubric.low: Information and budgeting enquiries with no time pressure, and spam.
urgency_rubric.caveat: SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION in src/classifier.py only defines what makes an email high urgency. The medium/low split above is this file's convention, so expect urgency accuracy to trail category accuracy until the prompt states the full rubric.

cases.note: Active leak from a NEW customer. None of the five categories fits a first-time emergency repair request: it is not a complaint about our work, and the sender wants help rather than a quote. Expecting 'general' documents the gap. If the model answers quote_request that is also defensible, and the taxonomy is what needs fixing, not the model.

cases.note: Apologetic, understated tone describing active water ingress above an infant's room, with more rain forecast. Tests that politeness does not mask urgency.

cases.note: No name, phone, address, or signature. The From address is the only contact detail available; every other customer field must come back empty rather than invented.
